streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan specifies single stream with all reagents dissolved. Concentration 0.1 M from batch input. Flow rate 0.5 mL/min from Engineering Design Calculations Step 3.

mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan stream_logic indicates all reagents are dissolved together before irradiation. No mixing of separate streams is required.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas carbon tetrachloride solution via sparging with inert gas (N2 or Ar) or membrane degasser to remove oxygen, as radical reactions are oxygen-sensitive (Chemistry Plan).
post_reactor_steps: Collect product stream. Note: Carbon tetrachloride is toxic; ensure proper waste handling.
chemistry_notes: Radical bromination of amino acid derivative using NBS and UV light. Single stream design. Oxygen sensitivity requires degassing. UV light (365 nm) initiates radical chain. Flow intensification reduces residence time from 8 h to ~12 min. Carbon tetrachloride solvent requires careful handling. No BPR required as T=30C is well below solvent boiling point and no gas is generated.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Engineering Design Calculations Step 2 estimated 12.3 min based on kinetic analogy blending (IF=39x). This is within the calculated range [6.7-24.0] min. Analogy 1 (3.75 min) and Analogy 2 (1 min) showed much shorter times but used different mechanisms/catalysts; our reaction is thermal/UV radical without photocatalyst, so we rely on the calculated kinetic estimate.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Single phase liquid system. Basis is liquid volume / liquid flow.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 30 C from batch input. Engineering Design Calculations Step 7 confirms thermal safety (Da_th = 0.001).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering Design Calculations Step 8 states BPR not required. T=30C is safe for CCl4 (bp ~77C). No gas generation.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: FEP selected for UV transparency (Photocatalysis rule) and chemical compatibility with CCl4. Analogy 2 used PFA, but FEP is generally more transparent to UV.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M from batch input. Analogy 1 used 0.03 M, Analogy 2 used 0.2 M. 0.1 M is a reasonable compromise and matches batch.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.5 mL/min from Engineering Design Calculations Step 3.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 6.15 mL from Engineering Design Calculations Step 3 (V = t * Q = 12.3 min * 0.5 mL/min).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm from Engineering Design Calculations Step 3. Consistent with Analogy 2 (0.5 mm) and general photochem guidelines (0.5-2.0 mm).
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 365 nm from Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm. Analogy 1 and 3 used 450 nm (blue LED), but our reaction uses UV light for NBS activation, so 365 nm is appropriate.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: UV LED array to provide 365 nm irradiation. Analogy 1 and 3 used LED arrays.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Chemistry Plan states oxygen_sensitive: true. Sparging or membrane degassing is standard for flow radical reactions.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: Radical bromination in flow, 3.75 min residence time, 450 nm LED. Key difference: Our reaction uses UV (365 nm) and no photocatalyst, so residence time is longer (12.3 min vs 3.75 min).

Analogy 2: Photoredox radical substitution, 1 min residence time, PFA tubing. Key difference: Our reaction is not photoredox catalyzed, so residence time is longer. Tubing material FEP preferred for UV transparency.
Analogy 3: Photocatalyzed radical addition, 2.5 min residence time, 450 nm LED. Key difference: Our reaction uses UV light and no catalyst, so residence time is longer.
